Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation  NovaPay

Hi Samantha / Tom 

Thanks again for taking time today. Wanted to capture the key takeaways from our discovery call and confirm next steps so we can put together a targeted proposal. Please flag anything I got wrong.

High-level pain points
- Recent incidents (2 in last 3 months) caused payment processing degradation for ~10-12 minutes and triggered manual failover.
- Primary concerns: deterministic latency under peak (end-to-end p95 target < 300ms for model calls), predictable throughput during batch settlements, and safe graceful degradation (no total outage for downstream systems).
- Regulatory/data residency: some payment flows and logs must remain in-region (US) and encrypted at rest.

Current stack (from call)
- Core payments: on-prem PCI-certified stack for authorization.
- ML: model scoring runs in AWS us-east-1 via vendor X today; using a mixture of hosted embeddings + an internal inference service for routing.
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra alerts, but historically model inference incidents have been noisy to triage (KV-cache misses + cold-start spikes).

Success criteria / what NovaPay needs to see to move forward
1) Demonstrated reliable failover path: multi-region fallback or model variant fallback that keeps p95 < 500ms during degraded conditions.
2) Clear SLOs: target uptime and latency bounds for API under committed capacity (we discussed 99.9% monthly for critical endpoints).
3) Auditable incident timeline and runbook for model failures, including automated rollback and canary policies.
4) Data controls: KMS integration and region-restricted logging for sensitive flows.

Incident history (summary from Tom)
- 2026-01-28: KV cache invalidation during deploy led to 12m tail latency increase.
- 2026-02-16: Downstream rate limiter misconfiguration; model endpoints saturated during a settlement window.

Proposed next steps (agreed)
- Redwood to produce a short proposal (2-3 pages) describing: (a) fallback model options (quantized warm-standby; smaller checkpoint for emergency fallback), (b) multi-region routing plan (primary us-east-1, standby us-west-2 / eu-west-1 for specific non-sensitive flows), (c) SLOs and canary rollout approach, and (d) high-level cost delta for reserved vs burst capacity.
- Please send redacted incident logs (timestamps + metrics) for the two incidents so our infra team can run a quick post-mortem.
- Schedule a 45-minute technical follow-up with Jonas (infra/architecture) and your security contact to walk through SOC2/KMS and network/topology questions.

Suggested times: Mar 18-19 (10am-2pm PT)  - if those don't work, propose alternatives.

Attachments: 2026-03-15-incident-timeline.pdf (redacted timeline stub)

Thanks —

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 12:22:30 -0700
Subject: Internal: NovaPay  - quick tech notes ahead of Wed proposal

Marissa / Rachel  - notes from my pass on the call and prep items for the proposal/demo. Keeping this internal so we can be candid about tradeoffs.

Summary of technical asks
- Hard SLO target: they want p95 < 300ms under normal conditions, p95 < 500ms in degraded scenarios. They mentioned desire for 99.9% but we should scope with reserved capacity numbers (99.8-99.9 range depending on reservation).
- Graceful degradation options:
  1) Model-variant fallback: primary large model -> quantized warm-standby (same arch, 4-bit q) for emergency; pros: minimal behavior delta, cons: cold-start risk unless KV warm/standby memory pinned.
  2) Regional fallback: route non-sensitive flows to standby region (us-west-2) with cached prefixes for settlement windows; pros: resilience to region outage, cons: regulatory gating for decisioning data.
  3) Hybrid: keep small local on-prem/edge policy for absolute critical decisions (simple rules) + remote model for enrichments.

Capacity & perf numbers (rough estimates)
- Under reserved capacity config (2x p100-equivalent fleet): p50 per-token latency ~15ms, p95 ~120-180ms for short-form scoring (<=256 tokens). With simultaneous bursts during settlement we see p95 creeping toward 350-450ms unless we enable pre-warming and aggressive batching  - which adds cost.

Rollback/canary proposal
- Canary: deploy to 5% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor error rate and latency; automated rollback trigger if error rate > 0.5% or p95 increase > 50% vs baseline.
- Fallback activation: automatic switch to warm-standby model variant when sustained error/backpressure detected for > 60s; route with circuit-breaker and gradual traffic shift (10% increments).

Prep items for proposal/demo
- Need redacted incident logs (timestamps, error codes, request rates)  - helps us replicate.
- Confirm whether they can accept warm standby in us-west-2 for non-PII flows.
- I'll prepare a short demo showing failure injection and automatic fallback (30min) to run during the Mar 19 session.

Attachments in our draft: 2026-03-15-mvp-sla-proposal.xlsx (cost/SLO scenarios)
